article:
A save point with a URL

Git is versions. GitHub is the copy on the internet other tools can see. Vercel, Xcode, a friend, you on a different laptop — they all pull from that copy. If it only lives on your Desktop, it is a hobby that can vanish.

You do not need to “learn git.” You need a repo, a main branch, and the habit of putting the current truth there.

The words that matter

Repository: the project folder as the internet knows it. Commit: a save with a sentence. Push: send the save to GitHub. Pull: bring GitHub’s copy back. Branch: a spare copy if you are scared to touch main. For a long time you can live on main.

A README is a note on the door. Write one sentence about what the thing is. That is enough.

How I actually do it

bohobond/bohobond is this site. The tape, the chapters, the Play frame — they are files in that repo. The edit key on this page writes back through GitHub. That is the whole CMS. No WordPress. A token with permission to touch Contents, and a function that commits.

When something is wrong in production, I look at the last commit first. Not at my feelings.

Where noobs get stuck

Making a repo per file. Never pushing. Pushing keys. Or treating GitHub like a social network and spending a week on a profile instead of one project that runs.

Private is fine while it is ugly. Public is fine when you can stand a stranger cloning it. Either way, push.

Film this

Empty repo. First file. Commit message that is a human sentence. Refresh GitHub. Then show Vercel pointing at that repo. The chain should be visible in one take.

Do this before chapter 06

  • Make one repo for the tiny product from chapter 01.
  • Put the files in it. Push.
  • Write a one-line README.
  • Do not put a key in the repo. If you already did, delete it and make a new key.

Next: hosting — the button that turns a folder into a website.
